ambulances have their sirens on and the sounds produced are identical and have a constant frequency.

parts.text: Half of a stationary circular loop of radius r lies in a uniform magnetic field directed into the page. Over time Δt the field increases uniformly from B₀ to 4B₀. Derive the magnitude of the induced emf and determine the direction of current around the loop.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: A loop of resistance R has a constant emf ε = 3πr²B₀/(2Δt) across it for a time Δt. The quantities r, B₀ and Δt are constants. Derive the total energy dissipated in the loop during this interval.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: A circular wire loop lies in the page. Its left half is inside a uniform field directed into the page; its right half is outside the field. An anticlockwise current flows around the loop. State and explain the direction of the resultant magnetic force on the loop.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: A circular conducting loop is pulled across a straight boundary into a region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane. The field is constant in time. Explain whether an emf is induced (a) while the loop is entering the region and (b) while it continues moving wholly within the region.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: A glass block has a semicircular recess of radius R, filled with air. The refractive indices are n_g > 1 for glass and 1 for air. Horizontal rays meet the curved glass–air boundary at height h above the circle’s centre line. Geometry gives sin i = h/R, where i is measured from the local normal. Sketch the refracted rays at A and B in the diagram. Then sketch sin r against h, including the range for which a refracted ray exists, and explain how the graph agrees with your ray sketch.

contexts.text: Diagram for this question.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: Monochromatic light of frequency f₀ crosses from glass of refractive index n_g into air of refractive index 1. Derive the increase in its wavelength in terms of f₀, n_g and c.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: You have a resistor X, an ideal battery, several known resistors, an ammeter and a voltmeter. Describe how to test graphically whether X is ohmic, including meter connections, how to obtain a range of readings, one way to reduce uncertainty, and the criterion used on the graph.

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
A battery of unknown emf ε and internal resistance r is connected in series with a known resistor R and an ideal ammeter. Readings are:
R / Ω: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60
I / mA: 58, 44, 31, 28, 22, 19
Choose axes that give a straight line, plot the data with a best-fit line, and use the graph to estimate r.

parts.label: whole
parts.text: Light of wavelength λ₀ ejects electrons from a metal of work function Φ. Derive their maximum speed in terms of λ₀, Φ, Planck’s constant h, the speed of light c and electron mass m_e. Predict how that maximum speed changes if the wavelength is increased but emission still occurs, and explain why.

Which is a reasonable estimate of the weight of an adult human?

B. 700 N
C. 70 000 N
D. 7 000 000 N

parts.text:
A quantity has units N s² m⁻¹. By considering force divided by acceleration, which physical quantity could it represent?

B. Force
C. Mass
D. Momentum

parts.text:
A ball falls from rest with negligible air resistance. Its fall distance s and time t are measured to determine g. The percentage uncertainty in s is negligible and that in t is 4%. What is the percentage uncertainty in g?

A. 2%
B. 4%
C. 8%
D. 16%

parts.text:
A car moves in the positive direction without reversing. Its initial speed is u. With constant acceleration a, it moves through displacement d and reaches speed v. Which expression gives u?

A. v − ad
B. √(v² − 2ad)
C. v + ad
D. v − ½ad²

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
A bicycle slows uniformly from 8 m s⁻¹ to 6 m s⁻¹ over 7 m. The same deceleration continues. How much farther does it travel before stopping?

A. 7 m
B. 9 m
C. 16 m
D. 21 m

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
A velocity–time graph has area A₁ above the time axis and area A₂ below it. Both A₁ and A₂ denote positive area magnitudes. Which expression gives the total displacement?

A. A₁ − A₂
B. (A₁ + A₂)/2
C. A₁ + A₂
D. A₂ − A₁

parts.text:
Which statement describes the weight of an object?

A. Its mass multiplied by its actual acceleration.
B. The resultant force when it falls at terminal velocity.
C. The force on it due to a gravitational field.
D. The property that resists a change in motion.

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
Which statement correctly gives the principle of conservation of momentum?

A. Momentum is constant in every elastic collision, regardless of external forces.
B. Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
C. Force equals the rate of change of momentum.
D. The total momentum of an isolated system remains constant.

parts.text:

A. Diagram A
B. Diagram B
C. Diagram C
D. Diagram D

Diagram for this question.

parts.text:
A skydiver is initially at terminal speed. Immediately after her parachute opens she has her greatest upward acceleration; its magnitude then decreases until she reaches a lower terminal speed. Compare times t₁ before opening, t₂ just after opening and t₃ at the new terminal speed. Which statements are correct?

1. Acceleration magnitude is greatest at t₂.
2. Drag has the same magnitude at t₁ and t₃.
3. Drag is greatest at t₁.

A. 1 and 2
B. 1 and 3
C. 2 only
D. 3 only

parts.text:
Two blocks approach each other and collide elastically in one dimension. Afterwards P moves left at 70 cm s⁻¹ and Q moves right at 20 cm s⁻¹. For such a collision, the relative approach speed equals the relative separation speed. Which pair of initial velocities is possible?

A. P: 10 cm s⁻¹ right; Q: 60 cm s⁻¹ left
B. P: 50 cm s⁻¹ right; Q: at rest
C. P: 20 cm s⁻¹ left; Q: 70 cm s⁻¹ right
D. P: 60 cm s⁻¹ right; Q: 30 cm s⁻¹ left

A. Diagram A
B. Diagram B

D. Diagram D

parts.text:
A uniform bar has mass M and length L. A pivot lies a distance x from its left end, with x < L/2. A small mass m is placed to the left of the pivot, a distance y from it, to balance the bar. Assume the required position is available. What is y?

A. xM/m
B. M(L − x)/m
C. M(L − 2x)/(2m)
D. (Lm − xM)/m

parts.text:
The mass and volume of a sample are changed. Which pair of changes must increase its density?

A. Mass decreases; volume decreases
B. Mass decreases; volume increases
C. Mass increases; volume decreases
D. Mass increases; volume increases

parts.text:
A solid object is fully submerged in the same liquid on Earth and on Mars. Its volume and the liquid density are unchanged. The gravitational field strengths are 9.81 N kg⁻¹ and 3.7 N kg⁻¹ respectively. What is the ratio of upthrust on Mars to upthrust on Earth?

A. 0.38
B. 1.0
C. 2.7
D. 3.6

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
A student derives kinetic energy from the work done by a constant resultant force F over displacement s. The object starts from rest and reaches speed v. The kinematic result v² = 2as and Newton’s-law result F = ma may be used. Which equation is NOT part of a valid derivation?

A. F = ma
B. W = Fs
C. E = ½Fs
D. v² = u² + 2as

parts.label: whole
parts.text:
A ball starts 2.4 m above the ground, strikes the ground and rebounds to 1.8 m above it. What is the magnitude of the single height change used to calculate its gravitational potential-energy change between the starting and finishing positions?

A. 0.6 m
B. 1.8 m
C. 2.4 m
D. 4.2 m

parts.text:
A block is pushed 8.0 m up a slope by a constant 1.8 N force parallel to the slope. It moves at constant speed. Friction dissipates 4.8 J, and the block’s weight is 4.0 N. How much vertical height does it gain?

A. 1.2 m
B. 2.4 m
C. 3.6 m
D. 4.8 m

parts.text:

A. 0.12 kW
B. 1.2 kW
C. 7.2 kW
D. 71 kW

parts.text:

A. Compression
B. Load
C. Fractional change in length
D. Force per unit area

parts.text:
A spring obeys Hooke’s law. Its extension rises linearly from zero at zero force to 4.0 cm at a force of 30 kN. What elastic potential energy is stored at this extension?

A. 60 J
B. 120 J
C. 600 J
D. 1200 J

parts.text:
Which statement correctly describes a progressive longitudinal mechanical wave?

A. Energy transfer is perpendicular to particle oscillations; no medium is required.
B. Energy transfer is perpendicular to particle oscillations; its speed is always the same.
C. Energy transfer is parallel to particle oscillations; no medium is required.
D. Energy transfer is parallel to particle oscillations; it requires a medium and its speed depends on that medium.

D. 3.5I

contexts.text: Diagram for this question.

B. 68 m s⁻¹ directly towards

parts.text:

A. Frequency decreases; speed increases

D. Frequency unchanged; speed unchanged

A. A position whose displacement is always at its maximum value
B. A position whose particles never move

D. A position of minimum oscillation amplitude

parts.text:
Two loudspeakers are connected to one signal generator. A listener moves across the region in front of them and hears repeated rises and falls in loudness. Which wave effect explains this?

A. Diffraction
B. Doppler shift
C. Interference
D. Reflection

C. 36 V

parts.text:

(a) Calculate the magnitude of her resultant force.
(b) State its direction.
(c) Sketch and label her weight and the total contact force from the ground. Explain how their vector sum gives the required resultant.

parts.text:

parts.label: whole
